The camera is bolted in place: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no handheld shake, no dolly, no cuts, no transitions, no slow motion, constant framing for the entire clip. Wide-angle lens, 16:9, 24 fps, real-time playback speed, realistic surveillance look with mild lens distortion and flat industrial color. No on-screen text, timestamps, or overlays.

Camera mounted 5 meters high in a corner, looking down at about 35 degrees. Scene: pump skid area on an offshore platform. Several waist-high pumps and motors on steel skid frames, pipes running at knee and waist height, a control panel on a post, grey steel deck plate with yellow walkway markings. Hazy morning with light sea mist, low contrast, soft grey light, damp glistening deck.

Workers wear orange or red flame-resistant coveralls, white or yellow hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, and steel-toe boots. Every worker stays fully in frame, full body visible head to boots, between 4 and 12 meters from the camera, never cropped by the frame edge, never fully hidden by equipment for more than a few frames.

Scenario: a worker sees a small leak dripping from a pump fitting near the deck, quickly gets down onto his hands and knees in front of the pump, and wipes the deck with a rag while leaning close to the fitting. After a few seconds he sits back on his heels, then stands. A second worker walks over and stands beside him looking down at the pump.

Nobody falls. Every movement is deliberate, controlled and at natural real-life speed, not slow motion: workers get down to the deck and back up on purpose, the way experienced crew do during routine maintenance. Clip length 10 seconds, continuous single take. The main action starts after about second 2 and is clearly visible.
